judgments.reasoning_cat1: A run-together heading ('THISFARMOUTAGREEMENTDATED') and spacing errors are OCR-level noise that do not change meaning; the parties, date and defined roles are plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The promise that the Agreement 'shall be effective as hereinafter provided' sits against Section 17, which simply makes it 'effective as of the date first above written', so the deferred-effectiveness signal is never cashed out but also does no work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: a $2,000 fee payable concurrently with execution, with amount, payee and timing all specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This payment obligation appears only in a recital; the operative text (Section 3(B)(2)) prices only Subsequent Well location fees, so a court could be asked whether the recital creates an enforceable term — a classic 2.3 posture.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'all rights associated with' the 2000' radius area around Well KF-1053 is a broad, unbounded reservation, though the geographic boundary itself is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Section 2(D)'s exclusion and the Exhibit 'A' footnote, so it harmonises; the only friction is that it is a recital stating what Farmee 'may acquire' against operative earning provisions in Section 3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure list of exhibits with one-line descriptions; nothing in it can bear two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit 'C' is titled a 'Geological Requirement Letter' but is drafted as requirements on an undefined 'Operator', and Section 3(D) makes compliance with it a condition of earning — a mismatch, but one that lives in Exhibit C rather than here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining a 'completed well' to include a well 'plugged and abandoned, if a dry hole' is counter-intuitive, and 'fully equipped for the taking of production' is a standard-laden phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The operative text never uses the defined term 'completed well', speaking instead of a well 'completed as a well capable of production in paying quantities' (Sections 3(B), 3(D)), leaving the definition orphaned and the 45-day Completion/Plugging Deadline measured against an unused standard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'e.g.' list (spacing unit, unit for production, proration unit) is illustrative rather than exhaustive, but the governing criterion — boundaries set by the regulatory authority — is objective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Sections 3(A)(1) and 3(B)(1), which allow drilling on 'a drilling unit that includes all or a portion of Farmout Lands'; no conflicting definition appears elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is circular — an 'earning well' is a well by which Farmee is entitled to an Assignment — but it is short and its referent is Section 3(D).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined term 'earning well' is not used anywhere in the operative text or exhibits, so it neither conflicts with nor supports any provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describing an area as an '80 acre circle' / '40 acre circle' and pegging the grant to a well 'capable of producing in paying quantities' imports two contestable notions — circle radius derived from acreage, and paying quantities — into the core grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3(E) fixes earned depths by footage while Exhibit D's granting clause leaves the acre-circle blank and Exhibit D's last reservation excepts strata below a blank 'formation', so the extent of what is earned must be reconciled across three provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'and other similar burdens on production' is a general catch-all appended to an enumerated list — the paradigm ejusdem generis question about how far 'similar' reaches.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined term 'lease burdens' is never used in the operative sections or exhibits, so the catch-all has no operative consequence to conflict with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A purely numerical definition — surface to 4,000' — with no evaluative language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision actually obliges Farmee to drill to Contract Depth, yet Section 3(C) presupposes wells being 'drilled to Contract Depth' and Section 3(E) caps earned depths at the same 4,000', so the term's role in the earning scheme is not fully worked out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the initial well drilled pursuant to the terms and conditions contained herein' is definite and single-referent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Section 3(A), which names the well Farmee 'shall drill' the 'test well'; nothing elsewhere competes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'capable of producing in commercial quantities' introduces an undefined standard that differs from the 'paying quantities' test used throughout the rest of the instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7(A) imposes shut-in royalties on any capable well shut in 'whether or not such well has already produced', which directly contradicts this definition's requirement that a shut-in well 'has previously produced'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading word is mistyped ('subseauent'), and the definition keys on any well drilled after completion of the test well rather than on the Section 3(B) specifications.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3(B) treats 'Subsequent Wells' as wells drilled 'strictly in accordance with' its own specifications, so a well drilled later but outside those specifications sits awkwardly between the two texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical residual definition keyed entirely to whether Operating Rights have been earned.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on Section 2(D)/3(D) for content and is used consistently in Sections 3(B)(1) and 5(B); no competing usage found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the cost of drilling, completing and equipping said well' does not say whose costs, whether operating or overhead costs count, or how gross proceeds are measured against them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Payout is the trigger for the royalty escalations in Section 4.A, so any looseness in the definition transmits directly into the money term, but the two texts do not contradict each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Farmee's choice on Farmout Land' is deliberately open, and a completion deadline running 45 days from 'reaching total depth' has no deadline for reaching total depth in the first place.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13(A) says the Agreement terminates 'pursuant to Section[] 3(A)(2)', but 3(A)(2) contains no termination language at all — the termination consequence has to be imported from Section 3(F).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The drafting is self-contradictory: Farmee 'shall have the option' to drill Subsequent Wells, yet 'must commence' two by December 31, 1996, and then 'at Farmee's further option, it shall continuously develop' — 'option' and 'shall' in the same breath.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13(A) treats 3(B)(3) as a termination trigger for failure 'to meet the drilling commitments', and Section 3(F) terminates on any failure to commence or continue drilling, which cannot be squared with an optional continuous-development programme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'lost for any reason' and a 'formation or condition which would render further drilling impractical or impossible' are judgment-laden triggers resting on Farmee's own assessment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is not stated whether commencing a substitute well satisfies the fixed spudding deadlines in 3(A)(2) and 3(B)(3) or merely preserves rights, and Section 3(F) makes time of the essence for those very deadlines.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The condition is Farmor's subjective state — 'after Farmor is satisfied that Farmee has complied with all its obligations' — coupled with an open-ended 'including but not limited to' catch-all and a harsh forfeiture.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 60-day clock in (2) runs from completion while the 60-day clock in the opening runs from Farmor's satisfaction, and Section 2(C)'s 'earning well' and Exhibit D's form must be read alongside; the pieces fit only loosely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise numerical formula — surface to 100' below total depth, capped at 4,000' — with nothing evaluative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D reserves everything below a blank '____ formation' rather than below the footage line drawn here, and Section 2(D) defines the earned estate areally, so the vertical extent of what is assigned is described three different ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If Farmee defaults, other than above' is an imprecise carve-out, and the section mixes automatic termination with a 30-day notice-and-cure regime without saying which failures fall where.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with Section 3(B)'s optional development programme, Section 13(A)'s list of termination triggers, and Section 6's takeover machinery, and the automatic-termination sentence sits uneasily with the cure right that follows.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proportionate-reduction sentence is garbled — 'less than one hundred percent (100%) or the working interest' — and 'Farmor reserves the right to escalate' leaves it unclear whether escalation is automatic on Payout or a discretionary election.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D's royalty paragraph says Assignor 'shall bear its proportionate part of any severance tax', which contradicts this section's 'without deductions of any kind', and Exhibit D contains no escalation mechanism at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'ceases production' has no duration qualifier and 'immediately give Farmor written notice' is undefined, though the 30-day and 48-hour response windows are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5(B) speaks of plugging 'without written notification and Farmor's approval', whereas this section makes Farmor's silence an election not to take over — approval is never required here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'without written notification and Farmor's approval' is ambiguous in its conjunction, and 'a reasonable opportunity to consider its options' is a vague alternative trigger for forfeiture.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5(A) gives Farmor only a right, not an approval power, and deems non-response an election not to take over, so this clause's 'approval' requirement cannot be located anywhere in 5(A).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any Operating Rights Earned by Farmor and earned by Farmee' is grammatically broken, and 'estimated salvage value ... less estimated plugging costs' leaves the estimator unnamed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3(F) and 5(B) preserve Farmee's Operating Rights Earned notwithstanding default, while this section requires Farmee to assign 'any Operating Rights Earned' on takeover — a genuine tension over earned rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text contains a typographic run-together ('for any reasontfor'), and a royalty of '$500.00 per well per year, prorated on a monthly basis' payable 'by the last day of each month' is arithmetically opaque.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies to a well capable of production 'whether or not such well has already produced', which cannot be squared with the Section 2(H) definition of 'shut-in well' as one that 'has previously produced'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Wheri possible' is a typo for 'When possible', and the qualifier makes the notice obligation dependent on an unmeasurable feasibility standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a soft adjunct to 7(A) and to the Section 10 notice machinery; no other provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is a long, carefully drafted indemnity whose 'including but not limited to' lists are illustrative; the only real question is the absence of any carve-out for Farmor's own conduct.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D contains a parallel indemnity from Assignee to Assignor covering the same operations, and Section 11 requires insurance naming Farmor; these stack rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'free and clear from all liens' is absolute and unqualified, with no carve-out for statutory or contested liens.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15(D) permits liens with Farmor's consent and Exhibit D expressly gives Assignor a lien on future production for unpaid royalty, so an absolute no-lien covenant sits oddly with both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'does not warrant title, either express or implied' is grammatically inverted (warranties, not title, are express or implied), though the disclaiming intent is unmistakable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D repeats a fuller disclaimer of all warranties, and Section 12 nonetheless asserts Farmor's retained interests in after-acquired rights; the two are compatible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The confidentiality period is fixed at one year 'after any such well is completed', which depends on the contested Section 2(A) definition of completion but is otherwise definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It routes well notices to Exhibit 'C', which addresses obligations to an undefined 'Operator' and a different addressee than Section 10(B); a minor seam rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure contact details with no operative standard; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit C, D.1 directs reports to a different attention line (Mike Stamper) than this clause (Lester Zitkus), but Section 10(A) expressly channels well data through Exhibit C, so the two coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insurance covenant names types of coverage but no limits, deductibles or duration, leaving 'acquire and/or maintain' adequate coverage unmeasured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements the Section 8(A) indemnity and nothing elsewhere sets competing insurance terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading 'Modifications and Amendments' does not describe the text, which is an after-acquired-interest clause; 'any subsequently acquired interest in such lands' is broad and undefined in scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It extends Farmor's reserved royalty to interests Farmee obtains 'directly or indirectly', which brushes against Section 9's disclaimer of title and Section 4.A's reservation mechanics without squarely contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The term is defined only by cross-reference, and the two limbs leave no stated outcome for the ordinary case where some lands are earned and Farmee simply stops drilling without default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites Sections 3(A)(2) and 3(B)(3) as provisions under which the Agreement 'terminates', but neither contains any termination language — the trigger exists only in 3(F) — and Section 4.A's royalty is said to survive termination.
